2/04.12.2025 Heard learned counsel appearing on behalf of Petitioner and learned counsel appearing on behalf of the State.
2.

The petitioner is apprehending his arrest in connection with Pindrajora P.S. Case No. 30 of 2024,
registered under Sections 406, 420, 467, 468, 471 & 120B of the Indian Penal Code, pending before the court of learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class, Bokaro.

3. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the petitioner happened to be the purchaser of the land in question on payment of consideration amount of Rs.14,60,000/- and the allegation is made that title of seller is in dispute.
He then submits that the witnesses on the sale-deed have been granted anticipatory bail in ABA No.6559 of 2024.
He next submits that the petitioner has got no criminal antecedent as disclosed in Para 9 of the petition.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the State opposed the prayer and submits that the allegations are there that the title of the said land is in dispute.

sentences.text:

1 5.

Considering that the petitioner is the purchaser of the land in question on payment of consideration amount of Rs.14,60,000/- and 2025:JHHC:36402 the witnesses on the sale-deed have been granted anticipatory bail in aforesaid ABA and the petitioner has got no criminal antecedent; I am inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

6. Accordingly, the petitioner above named is directed to surrender before the learned Court within three weeks from the date of receipt of the order and on the event of his surrender / arrest, he shall be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Twenty-Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount of each to the satisfaction of learned Judicial Magistrate, 1st Class,
Bokaro, in connection with Pindrajora P.S. Case No. 30 of 2024, subject to the condition as laid down under Section 482(2) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
7. This Anticipatory Bail Application is accordingly allowed and disposed of.
(Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi, J.) 04.12.2025
